summary: Gone Divide Mountain lookout, Glacier County, MT: 1931 ready-cut house wrecked by wind; 1934 octagon replacement; foundation remains as of 2022.

facts.design: Original 14-by-14 ready-cut lookout house on a stone foundation with cable guys; replacement was an octagon
facts.status_note: Original house demolished by wind in November 1931. Octagon cab collapsed over winter 2021-22; foundation remains as of 2022 per firetower.org
facts.agency: National Park Service (administers the site); Blackfeet Nation (cooperator)

events.note: June 1931 ready-cut 14 x 14 lookout house on the east slope, per the Blackfeet Reservation annual forestry report. firetower.org says a foundation was constructed in 1931.
November 1931 windstorm demolished the lookout building, leaving the floor and the north wall.

The 1932 report planned an observer from July 25 until the high fire hazard ended (about September 10), to live about half a mile away in a tent the agency would supply. Planned only; the sources do not confirm it was carried out.
firelookout.com says the octagonal cab was built about 1932. Conflicts with the 1934 date in the forestry report and firetower.org.
Replacement lookout completed in FY1934 to replace the one destroyed by wind. firetower.org says the second lookout was an octagon built in 1934.
Octagonal cab collapsed over the winter of 2021/2022 after years of abandonment (firelookout.com). firetower.org: as of 2022 the structure was destroyed by wind and the foundation remains.
Date registered December 25, 2022; nominated by Michael Wharton.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com says the octagon cab was built about 1932; the 1934 forestry report and firetower.org say the replacement was completed or constructed in 1934. The story gives 1934 and notes the disagreement.
firelookout.com's header reads R.I.P. 1938-2022, which conflicts with the 1931 and 1934 records. The story does not use 1938.

firetower.org says wind destroyed the structure as of 2022 and the foundation remains. firelookout.com says it collapsed over winter 2021/2022. The story gives both without assigning a cause. The NPS article, last updated August 12, 2025, calls Divide Lookout one of the few left from Moe's era; that conflicts with the other two pages, and the story flags the conflict without resolving it.

notes_for_editor: Brief says NPS-administered with 1931 build and 2022 registration; both confirmed. Build and replacement dates conflict (1931 house; 1932 vs 1934 octagon; 1938 header). The NPS article (cached copy, last updated August 12, 2025) calls Divide Lookout one of the few left from Moe's era, which conflicts with firetower.org and firelookout.com; the story flags the conflict and does not resolve it, so check the NPS page before relying on any 'today' description. No source gives current public access; the story omits it. Foundation is the only remains described (firetower.org, as of 2022). Firetower.org mentions a 2022 photo by Michael Wharton and firelookout.com credits photos to Mark Hufstetler and Luke Channer, but neither page gives a usable image URL, so no photos were added. Page-read budget used up; no WebSearch beyond one websearch.py query. The 1932 observer and the 1934 lookout station were planned in the reports, not confirmed, so the staffing fact was dropped and the 1932 event is marked as planned.
